questions.question: Which lighthouses in historic county Cornwall does the table name an architect for who, according to the engineers file, was born before 1800?
questions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT l.name FROM lighthouses l, (SELECT qid, unnest(string_split(architect, '; ')) AS who FROM lighthouses) a, engineers e WHERE a.qid = l.qid AND e.name = a.who AND year(e.birth) < 1800 AND l.historic_county = 'Cornwall'
questions.note: Joins the table's architect cell to engineers.json. Born before 1800: John Smeaton (1724), Daniel Asher Alexander (1768), James Walker (1781); James Nicholas Douglass (1826) is not. The Cornish lighthouses with Walker as architect are Trevose Head, Godrevy, Wolf Rock and Bishop Rock (the last two also name Douglass); no Cornish lighthouse names Smeaton or Alexander. The question reads the table's architect cell: the St Anthony's Lighthouse article says it was designed by James Walker, but its architect cell is empty, so St Anthony's is not in the answer.

questions.question: The Farne Lighthouse article names the man who designed the pair of lighthouses built on Inner Farne in 1811. In what year did he die, according to the engineers file?

chunks.quote: both of which were designed by Daniel Alexander

questions.sql: SELECT year(death) FROM engineers WHERE name = 'Daniel Asher Alexander'
questions.note: memorisable: The article says Daniel Alexander; the engineers file holds him as Daniel Asher Alexander (died 1846-03-02), the table's architect of Farne Lighthouse.

questions.question: The Godrevy Lighthouse article names the man contracted to design the lighthouse. How many lighthouses in the table name him as their architect?

chunks.quote: with James Walker contracted to design the lighthouse

questions.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM lighthouses WHERE list_contains(string_split(architect, '; '), 'James Walker')
questions.note: The article names James Walker (James Sutcliffe was the project's engineer, not its designer). The table names Walker as architect of South Foreland Upper, Trevose Head, Start Point, Coquet, Needles, Whitby, Godrevy, Wolf Rock and Bishop Rock; the last two also name James Nicholas Douglass and count once each.

questions.question: The St Mary's Lighthouse article compares its first-order optic with one Barbier & Bénard had supplied the year before to another lighthouse. Which kinds of event does the events file record for that other lighthouse?

chunks.quote: very similar to the one they had provided the previous year for Lundy North Lighthouse

questions.sql: SELECT event FROM events WHERE lighthouse.name = 'Lundy North Lighthouse'
questions.note: memorisable: The other lighthouse is Lundy North Lighthouse. The events file gives it electrification (1971), automatization (1976) and conversion to solar power (1991).

questions.question: According to the Whitby Lighthouse article, the lantern and optic of the demolished Whitby North Light were re-used at a new lighthouse. In what year does the table record that lighthouse's service retirement?

chunks.quote: its lantern and optic both went on to be re-used at a new lighthouse then being built at Withernsea

questions.sql: SELECT CAST(service_retirement AS INTEGER) FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'Withernsea Lighthouse'
questions.note: memorisable: The new lighthouse is Withernsea Lighthouse; its service_retirement cell is 1972. The article gives no date for Withernsea.

questions.question: According to the St Agnes Lighthouse article, which lighthouse superseded St Agnes in 1911? Give the light characteristic the table records for that lighthouse.

chunks.quote: having been superseded by Peninnis Lighthouse

questions.sql: SELECT light_characteristic FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'Peninnis Lighthouse'
questions.note: memorisable: St Agnes was superseded by Peninnis Lighthouse, whose light_characteristic cell is 'Fl W 20s'. The article calls Peninnis a 17-metre tower while the table's height is 14; the question avoids height.

questions.question: The Whitby Lighthouse article says trials of different fog signals were held at another lighthouse in 1901. How many lighthouses in the table lie in the same historic county as that lighthouse, itself included?

chunks.quote: Following trials of different types of signal (conducted at St. Catherine's Lighthouse in 1901)

questions.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM lighthouses WHERE historic_county = (SELECT historic_county FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'St. Catherine''s Lighthouse')
questions.note: The trials were at St. Catherine's Lighthouse, historic county Hampshire (its located_in cell names the Isle of Wight, its county cell Hampshire). The table's Hampshire rows are Hurst Point, St. Catherine's, Needles, Nab Tower and Egypt Point.

questions.question: The Old Higher Lighthouse article says Portland High was again made a fixed light after another lighthouse was established with revolving Fresnel lenses. How many events does the events file record for the lighthouses in that lighthouse's historic county?

chunks.quote: establishment of Start Point Lighthouse with its revolving Fresnel lenses, Portland High was again made a fixed light

questions.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM events e JOIN lighthouses l ON l.qid = e.lighthouse.qid WHERE l.historic_county = (SELECT historic_county FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'Start Point Lighthouse')
questions.note: The other lighthouse is Start Point Lighthouse, historic county Devon. The events of Devon lighthouses: Start Point electrification (undated), Bull Point automatization (1975), Berry Head automatization (1921), Lundy North electrification, automatization and conversion to solar power, Lundy South automatization and conversion to solar power: 8. Undated events count; eight of the 13 Devon rows have no event.

questions.question: The Farne Lighthouse article says the 1811 light on Brownsman Island was later moved to another island and renamed. Which other lighthouses does the events file record as automated in the same year as that renamed lighthouse?

chunks.quote: named Longstone Lighthouse, it too remains active as an aid to navigation for Trinity House

questions.sql: SELECT lighthouse.name FROM events WHERE event = 'automatization' AND left(date, 4) = (SELECT left(date, 4) FROM events WHERE lighthouse.name = 'Longstone Lighthouse' AND event = 'automatization') AND lighthouse.name <> 'Longstone Lighthouse'
questions.note: The renamed light is Longstone Lighthouse, automatization 1990. The other automatization events dated 1990 are Cromer (1990), Coquet (1990) and the Casquets (1990-11). The two 'automation' rows have no date.

questions.question: Which historic county or counties have the most lighthouses in the table?
questions.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT historic_county, count(*) AS n FROM lighthouses WHERE historic_county IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) SELECT historic_county FROM c WHERE n = (SELECT max(n) FROM c)
questions.note: A tie: Cornwall and Devon have 13 lighthouses each, then Northumberland 8. Both are the answer; three rows have no historic county and are not counted.

questions.question: How many automation events in the events file are dated in the 1990s?
questions.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM events WHERE event IN ('automatization', 'automation') AND date LIKE '199%'
questions.note: 13 'automatization' events have a date from 1990 to 1999 (1990-11, 1994-02 and 1994-08 included). The two 'automation' rows (Lizard, Longships) have no date, so both labels give 13.

questions.question: Which engineer is named as architect of the most lighthouses in the table?
questions.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT unnest(string_split(architect, '; ')) AS who FROM lighthouses), c AS (SELECT who, count(*) AS n FROM a GROUP BY 1) SELECT who FROM c WHERE n = (SELECT max(n) FROM c)
questions.note: James Nicholas Douglass is architect of 12 lighthouses, James Walker of 9, John Smeaton and Daniel Asher Alexander of one each; cells with two names count for both.

questions.question: How many lighthouses have an electrification event in the events file?
questions.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT lighthouse.qid) FROM events WHERE event = 'electrification'
questions.note: 17 electrification rows, each for a different lighthouse; five of them (Lizard, Start Point, Peninnis, Wolf Rock, Round Island) have no date and still count.

questions.question: Which lighthouses have the most events in the events file?
questions.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT lighthouse.name AS name, count(*) AS n FROM events GROUP BY 1) SELECT name FROM c WHERE n = (SELECT max(n) FROM c)
questions.note: Both have three events (Lundy North: electrification, automatization, conversion to solar power; Bishop Rock: electrification, automatization, stiffening); no lighthouse has more.

questions.question: How many lighthouses does the table record with the material value 'stone' (alone or alongside another material)?
questions.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM lighthouses WHERE list_contains(string_split(material, '; '), 'stone')
questions.note: Counts every row whose material cell holds the value 'stone', alone or with another value (Longships, Needles and Round Island are 'stone; granite'). Not counted, although granite is a stone: the granite-only rows St Anthony's, Start Point and Bishop Rock, Wolf Rock's 'granite; concrete' and Europa Point's 'masonry'.

questions.question: Of the lighthouses the ten articles are about, which does its own article say had a fog signal sounded through Tannoy emitters or units?

chunks.quote: introduced, sounding from 35 Tannoy emitters
The fog signal was originally a series (72 in total) of Tannoy units built into the lighthouse tower
sounded from a stack of thirty tannoy emitters

questions.note: St Anthony's (35 Tannoy emitters, 1954), Tater Du (72 Tannoy units) and Anvil Point (thirty tannoy emitters, 1960). The St Anthony's article adds that Trinity House installed this type at a dozen or so other lighthouses, which it does not name. Whitby used sirens through Rayleigh trumpets.

questions.question: Which lighthouse has the earliest dated automation event in the events file?

chunks.quote: In 1910 it was one of the first Trinity House lighthouses to be automated.

questions.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT lighthouse.name AS name, date FROM events WHERE event IN ('automatization', 'automation') AND date IS NOT NULL) SELECT name FROM a WHERE date = (SELECT min(date) FROM a)
questions.note: memorisable: Farne Lighthouse, automatization 1910; next are Berry Head (1921) and Hurst Point (1923). The Farne article agrees that it was automated in 1910.

questions.question: Of the lighthouses the ten articles are about, which does its own article say were converted to solar power?

chunks.quote: in 1996 the light was converted from acetylene to solar powered electric operation
In 1995, the lighthouse was modernised and converted to solar powered operation.

questions.note: Farne (1996, from acetylene to solar powered electric operation) and Godrevy (1995). The St Mary's article's 'first major lighthouse to be run using solar power' is the Inner Dowsing light platform, not St Mary's. The events file records solar conversions only for Lundy North and Lundy South, which have no article.

questions.question: Which lighthouses in historic county Northumberland does the table list as a Grade II listed building (not Grade II*)?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE historic_county = 'Northumberland' AND list_contains(string_split(heritage_designation, '; '), 'Grade II listed building')
questions.note: Coquet Lighthouse is Grade II* and is excluded; Heugh Hill, Bamburgh and Guile Point East have no designation.

questions.question: Of the lighthouses the ten articles are about, which first showed a light before 1800, according to their own articles?

chunks.quote: The light was first lit on 30 October 1680
they shone out for the first time on 29 September 1716

questions.note: St Agnes (first lit 30 October 1680) and Old Higher Lighthouse (with the Old Lower Lighthouse it first shone on 29 September 1716; both were rebuilt in 1869, which is the table's inception for Portland Bill High Light). Not counted: the earlier lights other lighthouses replaced, such as Captain Blackett's 1778 light on Inner Farne and the 1664 lighthouse at Tynemouth in the St Mary's article. The other eight were built from 1811 on.

questions.question: Which lighthouses in historic county Cornwall have no service retirement recorded in the table?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE historic_county = 'Cornwall' AND service_retirement IS NULL
questions.note: Of 13 Cornish rows, Lizard (1903), St Agnes (1911) and Godrevy (2012) have a retirement; the other ten are the answer. The question asks for the list: a count would be an aggregation question.

questions.question: Which lighthouses in the table have a red flashing light characteristic ('Fl R')?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE light_characteristic LIKE '%Fl R%'
questions.note: Souter 'Fl R 5s' and Hilbre Island 'Fl R 3s'. Characteristics with a white-red flash (Fl WR) are not 'Fl R'.

questions.question: Which lighthouses in historic county Cornwall does the table record as built of granite?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE historic_county = 'Cornwall' AND list_contains(string_split(material, '; '), 'granite')
questions.note: Material cells containing granite, alone or with stone or concrete. Start Point and Needles are granite too but in Devon and Hampshire.

questions.question: Which lighthouses in the table have an inception year before 1800?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE CAST(left(inception, 4) AS INTEGER) < 1800
questions.note: Lizard 1751, St Agnes 1680, Smeaton's Tower 1759, Happisburgh 1791, Casquets 1724, Orfordness 1793, North Foreland 1691. Read from the table's inception column, not from the older towers the articles describe (Portland Bill High Light's inception is 1869). The question asks for the list: a count would be an aggregation question.

questions.question: Which lighthouses does the table record as retired from service in the 1980s?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE CAST(left(service_retirement, 4) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1980 AND 1989
questions.note: service_retirement 1980-1989: South Foreland Upper 1988, Souter 1988, St. Mary's 1984, Spurn 1985, Egypt Point 1989.

questions.question: Which Grade II listed lighthouses in historic county Kent have no light characteristic in the table?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE historic_county = 'Kent' AND list_contains(string_split(heritage_designation, '; '), 'Grade II listed building') AND light_characteristic IS NULL
questions.note: Kent rows: South Foreland Upper and North Foreland have a characteristic, Dungeness is Grade II*; the remaining two qualify.

questions.question: Which lighthouses in the table are designated a scheduled monument?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE list_contains(string_split(heritage_designation, '; '), 'scheduled monument')
questions.note: Heritage cells containing 'scheduled monument', each alongside a listed-building grade.

questions.question: In what year does the table say Portland Bill Lighthouse, the current light at the Bill (not Portland Bill High Light or Portland Bill Low Light), entered service?
questions.sql: SELECT CAST(service_entry AS INTEGER) FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'Portland Bill Lighthouse'
questions.note: memorisable: service_entry 1906; its inception cell is 1903 and the Old Higher Lighthouse article says the new lighthouse was completed in 1905, so the question names the table's service entry. The High and Low Lights entered service in 1869.

questions.question: In what year does the table record the service retirement of South Foreland Lower Lighthouse?
questions.sql: SELECT CAST(service_retirement AS INTEGER) FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'South Foreland Lower Lighthouse'
questions.note: memorisable: 1904; South Foreland Upper Lighthouse, the other light of the pair, retired in 1988.

questions.question: Which heritage designation does the table give Dungeness Lighthouse, the tower in service since 1961, as opposed to Dungeness Old Lighthouse?
questions.sql: SELECT unnest(string_split(heritage_designation, '; ')) FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'Dungeness Lighthouse'
questions.note: memorisable: Dungeness Lighthouse (service entry 1961) is a Grade II* listed building; Dungeness Old Lighthouse, retired in 1961, is a Grade II listed building. Neither is a scheduled monument.

questions.question: In what year does the events file say Lundy South Lighthouse was converted to solar power?
questions.sql: SELECT CAST(date AS INTEGER) FROM events WHERE lighthouse.name = 'Lundy South Lighthouse' AND event = 'conversion to solar power'
questions.note: memorisable: 1994; Lundy North Lighthouse was converted in 1991, and Lundy Old Light has no events.

questions.question: What focal height, in metres, does the table give for Instow Rear Lighthouse?
questions.sql: SELECT CAST(focal_height_m AS DOUBLE) FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'Instow Rear Lighthouse'
questions.note: memorisable: 38; Instow Front Lighthouse, inception 1820 like the Rear, has 22.

questions.question: Which lighthouse does the table locate in St. Mary's?
questions.sql: SELECT name FROM lighthouses WHERE list_contains(string_split(located_in, '; '), 'St. Mary''s')
questions.note: Peninnis Lighthouse is located_in St. Mary's (the island in the Isles of Scilly). St. Mary's Lighthouse is a different lighthouse, located in North Tyneside.

questions.question: In what year does the table record the service retirement of Burnham-on-Sea Round Tower, as opposed to Burnham-on-Sea High Lighthouse?
questions.sql: SELECT CAST(service_retirement AS INTEGER) FROM lighthouses WHERE name = 'Burnham-on-Sea Round Tower'
questions.note: memorisable: 1832. The Round Tower's inception is 1801; Burnham-on-Sea High Lighthouse has inception 1832 and service retirement 1996, so confusing the two gives 1996.

questions.question: According to the Whitby Lighthouse article, how tall was the Whitby North Light, in metres?

chunks.quote: but taller at 20.5 m (67 ft)

questions.note: memorisable: 20.5 m (67 ft). The surviving South Light, the table's Whitby Lighthouse, has height 13 in the table; the article's North Light is the demolished twin.

questions.question: Of the lighthouses the ten articles are about, which does its own article describe as disused or decommissioned, no longer working as a lighthouse?

chunks.quote: The Old Higher Lighthouse is a disused 19th century lighthouse
While it no longer functions as a working lighthouse
In 1911 the St Agnes lighthouse was decommissioned
Godrevy is still listed by Trinity House as a lighthouse

questions.note: Old Higher (disused), St Mary's (decommissioned in 1984, no longer functions as a working lighthouse) and St Agnes (decommissioned in 1911, kept as a daymark). Not counted: Godrevy, whose light within the tower was discontinued in 2012 and replaced by an LED light nearby, but which is still listed by Trinity House as a lighthouse (the table's service_retirement 2012 is not what the question reads); and the discontinued fog signals or lenses of lighthouses that still work (Anvil Point, Tater Du).

questions.question: According to the Farne Lighthouse article, which of the two lighthouses built on Inner Farne in 1811 still functions as a lighthouse?

chunks.quote: it still functions as a lighthouse
use of the Low Light was discontinued

questions.note: memorisable: Farne Lighthouse, originally Farne High Lighthouse. Use of the other one, Farne Low Lighthouse, was discontinued after 1910 and it was demolished, so it does not count.

questions.question: According to the Tater Du Lighthouse article, which nearby cove does not allow dive-boats to launch from it?

chunks.quote: as Lamorna Cove just around the corner from The Bucks, does not allow launching from there

questions.note: memorisable: Lamorna Cove; Penzance is named as the nearest launching point, the opposite of the answer.

questions.question: In which years were earlier petitions to build a lighthouse on St Agnes submitted and refused, according to the St Agnes Lighthouse article?

chunks.quote: Earlier petitions to build a lighthouse on St Agnes (submitted by private individuals and companies in 1665
and 1679) had been refused.

questions.note: memorisable: The petitions of 1665 and 1679 were refused; the light that was built dates from 1680, which is not an answer. The sentence spans two chunks.

questions.question: In what year was a renovation plan for the St Mary's Lighthouse site rejected, according to its article?

chunks.quote: In 2017 a renovation plan for the site (including roof-top viewing platforms and various glass-covered extensions) was rejected by the local planning authority due to environmental concerns.

questions.note: memorisable: 2017, rejected by the local planning authority. The 2018 proposal was presented (its funding was later turned down) and the 2024 repairs were carried out; neither is the rejected plan.

questions.question: Of the lighthouses the ten articles are about, which does its own article say still sounds a fog signal today?

chunks.quote: The fog horn blasts once every 30 seconds.
but the fog signal was discontinued in 1988
The fog signal was decommissioned in 2012.
The fog bell was deactivated at the same time.
was operational from 1903 and continued in use until 1987

questions.note: St Anthony's: its Present day section says the fog horn blasts once every 30 seconds (its fog bell was decommissioned in 1954, replaced by the electric signal). Not counted, because their fog signals ended: Anvil Point (discontinued 1988), Tater Du (decommissioned 2012), Godrevy (fog bell deactivated in 1933) and Whitby (the fog signal station was in use until 1987). The other articles name no fog signal.

questions.question: According to the Old Higher Lighthouse article, which of the two Portland lights never had a revolving light?

chunks.quote: matching the Low Light, which had remained fixed throughout
In 1824 Portland High Light was improved by Trinity House: a three-sided revolving apparatus was installed

questions.note: memorisable: The Low Light remained fixed throughout; the High Light (Old Higher Lighthouse) had a revolving apparatus from 1824 until 1835. The article calls the low one the Old Lower Lighthouse; the table names it Portland Bill Low Light.

questions.question: Who opened Anvil Point Lighthouse, according to its article?

chunks.quote: It was opened by Joseph Chamberlain, the President of the Board of Trade.

questions.note: memorisable: Joseph Chamberlain, then President of the Board of Trade.

questions.question: Which Trinity House chief engineer designed and built Berry Head Lighthouse, according to its article?

chunks.quote: The lighthouse was designed and built for Trinity House by its chief engineer Thomas Matthews.

questions.note: memorisable: Thomas Matthews; the table names no architect for Berry Head and he is not in the engineers file.

questions.question: What did the construction of Godrevy Lighthouse cost, according to its article?

chunks.quote: Its construction took around a year at a cost of £7,082 15s 12d

questions.note: memorisable: The article's figure as written; a text answer for the judge because the pre-decimal sum has no single number form.

questions.question: Who bought the Old Higher Lighthouse in 1923, according to its article?

chunks.quote: Portland Museum founder Marie Stopes as a summer residence

questions.note: memorisable: Marie Stopes, as a summer residence.

questions.question: What was the name of the Spanish coaster whose loss led to the building of Tater Du Lighthouse?

chunks.quote: losing a small Spanish coaster called the Juan Ferrer on 23 October 1963

questions.note: memorisable: The Juan Ferrer, lost on 23 October 1963 off Boscawen Point with 11 lives.

questions.question: Which company built St Mary's Lighthouse in 1898, according to its article?

chunks.quote: by the John Miller company of Tynemouth

questions.note: memorisable: The John Miller company of Tynemouth; Barbier & Bénard supplied the optic, not the building.

questions.question: From how many Tannoy emitters did the experimental electric fog signal introduced at St Anthony's Lighthouse in 1954 sound?

chunks.quote: introduced, sounding from 35 Tannoy emitters

questions.note: memorisable: 35 emitters (Tater Du's later fog signal had 72 Tannoy units; Anvil Point's had thirty).

questions.question: For how many pounds was Farne Lighthouse sold to the National Trust, according to its article?

chunks.quote: Farne Island Lighthouse was sold on 6 June 2005 to the National Trust for £132,000

questions.note: memorisable: £132,000, on 6 June 2005; the building was leased back to Trinity House.
